title: Three native queries use MySQL-only syntax and fail on PostgreSQL
summary: Three of the 43 native SQL queries stop with a syntax error on PostgreSQL. Rewrite them, with a per-database version where no common form exists.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: The order service has 43 native SQL queries. The ORM does not write them, so they do not change with the database. Three of them use syntax that only MySQL accepts.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [READ] A search of the code found 3 MySQL-only forms: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, GROUP_CONCAT and LIMIT 40, 20. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] In staging, 40 queries pass. These 3 fail with a syntax error. [src: report.md]
  • [INFERRED] During the rollback window, the same release must run on MySQL and on PostgreSQL. Q3 has one form that both accept. Q1 and Q2 do not. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html:
• Q1 adds items to the cart. If Q1 fails, customers cannot buy.
  • Q2 feeds the nightly report.
  • Q3 pages the order search for the support team.

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html: Rewrite the 3 queries. Use LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40 for Q3, because both databases accept it. Keep a per-database version of Q1 and Q2. The service selects the version at start-up. Effort: 2 days.

tables_html:
QueryWhereMySQL formPostgreSQL form
Q1 cart upsertCartRepository.upsertLineON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE qty = qty + VALUES(qty)ON CONFLICT (cart_id, sku) DO UPDATE SET qty = cart_lines.qty + EXCLUDED.qty
Q2 SKU listNightlyReport.skuListGROUP_CONCAT(sku ORDER BY sku SEPARATOR ',')string_agg(sku, ',' ORDER BY sku)
Q3 search pageOrderSearch.pageLIMIT 40, 20LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40 (both databases)

options.label: Rewrite in SQL, with a per-database version of Q1 and Q2
options.detail_html: Effort: 2 days. Risk: low. The 3 queries keep their speed. The two versions of Q1 and Q2 stay in the code until the rollback window ends. Then remove the MySQL versions.

options.label: Move the 3 queries to the ORM query API
options.detail_html: Effort: 4 days. The ORM writes the SQL for each database. Risk: medium. The ORM has no upsert. Q1 becomes a read and then a write, with a race between parallel requests.

recommendation_html: Option a. It takes half the time, and it keeps the cart upsert atomic.
